name: Guangzhou Library
features: Stacked, cascading 'book' forms on the facade; the design concept is 'Beautiful Books'.
note: Wikipedia: new building opened 23 June 2013. Most other category photos are night shots, so only the daylight one is listed; it shows the main block but crops the right-hand wing.

name: Capital Museum
features: Stone-clad exterior wall meant to symbolise the city walls and towers of ancient China.
note: Wikipedia says the museum moved into its present building in 2006 (no separate completion date). A small bus and car sit in the foreground of the first photo.

name: Beijing Television Cultural Center (TVCC)
features: A continuous lobby gives access to a 1,500-seat theatre and public facilities under one folded volume.
note: Opened 16 May 2012 after a 2009 fire (infobox gives 2009). Check the TVCC isn't already on the wall under another name (taken.txt has CCTV only). The first photo is a tall portrait crop; the second has part of CCTV Headquarters on the right.

name: Wuhan Railway Station
by: AREP, Fourth Survey and Design Institute of China, MaP3, SNCF-IGOA
features: Nine separate parts stand for China's nine provinces; the roof takes its form from the yellow crane, Wuhan's symbol.

photos.file: File:20240621 West facade of Wuhan Railway Station.jpg

note: Won a two-phase competition in 2005; built 2006 to December 2009. The first photo is a wide panorama (3573x1588); the second has two small figures on the forecourt.

name: Tainan Art Museum
by: Sutejiro Umezawa; Shi Zhao Yong and Shigeru Ban
features: Ochre-tiled Art Deco building of 1930 beside a new wing shaped after Delonix regia, the royal poinciana.

photos.file: File:Tainan Art Museum Building 1 (台南市美術館1館）.jpg

note: Building 1 was the 1930 Tainan Police Department; the museum opened 27 January 2019. Only building 1 has a photo in the category listing I saw; building 2 (Ban) photos should be looked for in a sub-category.

name: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre
features: Glass curtain wall, the world's largest when built, looking over Victoria Harbour on three sides.
note: Old wing 1988, Topside 1989, New Wing 1994-97 (Wikipedia). Photo is from across the harbour, daylight; a Philips sign sits on a neighbouring tower behind it.

name: Hong Kong Central Library
features: Plan built from three shapes: the circle for sky, the square for land, the triangle for accumulated knowledge.
note: Opened 17 May 2001; Wikipedia names Ho Chiu-fan, a government senior architect, with Rocco Yim's alternative design not chosen. Photo is the front facade in daylight, trees in the lower part.

name: Shanghai Astronomy Museum
features: No straight lines or right angles; the forms express some of the fundamental laws of astrophysics.
note: Opened 2021 in Lingang. The second photo has the museum's name sign in the grass in front.

name: Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre
features: Daniel Libeskind's building for City University of Hong Kong's creative media school, designed with Leigh & Orange.

photos.file: File:Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre.JPG

note: Opened October 2011 in Kowloon Tong; Wikipedia says the design received several awards. Wikipedia gives few design details, so the features line is modest.

name: Shekou Cruise Center
features: Triangular terminal with 12 ferry berths and 2 cruise-ship berths.
note: Wikipedia: construction began 2014, new terminal due to open 1 November 2016. Photo shows the terminal from the water with two ferries in front.
